//providerReviewerAllowlist: Who may satisfy the cross-review, deliberately separate from the author list. It holds agent identities only: a human approval is a human approval, never a substitute for the counter provider's review.
//crossReviewResultAuthors: Trusted workflow identities that may publish a provider's structured, head-bound cross-review result when that integration does not submit a native GitHub review. This is deliberately not part of providerReviewerAllowlist.
//selfReviewResultAuthors: Trusted workflow identities that may publish a structured, head-bound self-review result on a provider's behalf, alongside resultAuthorsFor's manual identities (the provider's own bot account or its human operator running the local launcher). Kept separate for the same reason as crossReviewResultAuthors: a workflow identity is not itself one of the provider's own identities.
//reviewStartFailureAuthors: Trusted workflow identities that publish a head-bound start failure for either cross-review provider.
//reviewModeLabels: Set by the user, never by an agent: they decide who reviews the current head. The reconciler only removes one that was bound to an earlier head, so the choice is asked again per head SHA.
//statusCommentAuthors: Identities whose status comment may carry the review-mode binding. Narrower than the trusted-author check used to adopt a comment, because that one accepts every [bot] login and the binding decides whether an answer counts for this head.
//reviewDecisionNotificationAuthors: Only these identities may suppress the once-per-head active review-choice notification by publishing its machine-readable marker.
//codexDeliveryAuthors: Human identities whose GitHub acknowledgement proves that a Codex task message was sent successfully. The adapter posts this only after send_message_to_thread returns successfully.
//reviewWorkflowFiles: The trusted workflow file that runs a given reviewer provider's cross-review, keyed by `reviewerProvider` — never assembled from pull-request-controlled text. The reconciler dispatches it directly when a labeled attempt already declined for the current head only because the head was not ready yet, and the head has since become eligible.
//reviewRetriggerAuthors: Only these identities may suppress a further automatic re-dispatch by publishing its machine-readable marker.
//sensitivePathPrefixes: Paths that always make the recommendation fall back to the independent cross-review, regardless of how small the diff looks.
//crossReviewEvidence: What proves the counter provider reviewed the current head. `approval` demands a native approving review. `reviewed-and-resolved` accepts a native review of this exact head with no open findings, a credential-read-only structured result from a provider-specific trusted publisher, or a finding-free review the provider reported in a comment naming this exact head. An explicit changes-required result blocks under all of them.
//crossReviewEvidenceLimit: A native review is bound to its commit SHA by GitHub. A structured provider result must carry the exact SHA in the trusted review-result marker. A reported clean pass must name its reviewed commit in the comment and come from the configured reviewer identity; the Codex integration submits a review only when it has findings, so without this a clean pass would block a head it had just reviewed. Reactions remain deliberately excluded because they carry no SHA and could silently apply to a later head.
//selfReviewMinimumEnforcement: How strongly a self-review session must have been kept away from the code before its verdict opens the gate. `true` requires credentials without code write access — the strongest, but unreachable in environments whose only credentials can push. `verified` accepts a session the launcher ran with the editing tools removed in a throwaway worktree and checked afterwards to be untouched. `false` accepts a verdict nothing outside the prompt backed up and effectively turns the self-review gate into a formality.
